# Gromov Probability / Induction Source Corpus

This folder contains the local source corpus for Mikhail Gromov's probability
lectures and notes, with emphasis on finite sets, symmetry, subset algebras,
partitions/projections, cones of measures, entropy, large deviations, and
inductive/combinatorial probability.

## Primary Pages

- IHES official page:
  https://www.ihes.fr/~gromov/expository/586/
- Carmin collection:
  https://www.carmin.tv/en/collections/mikhael-gromov-probability-symmetry-linearity
- FGSI/EPFL event page, "What is Probability?":
  https://fgsi2019.sciencesconf.org/resource/page/id/5.html
- NYU/CIMS probability 2022-23 directory:
  https://cims.nyu.edu/~gromov/probability%202022-23/
- CNRS/CIRM probability/topology event:
  https://indico.math.cnrs.fr/event/7864/?print=1

## Downloaded Text Corpus

- `probability-huge-Lecture-Nov-2014.pdf`
- `CIMS_Probability_Topology_Lecture1_2022.pdf`
- `cims_probability_2022_23/*.pdf`

The CIMS mirror includes Pascal recursion, probability/topology, alternative
probabilities, entropy, cubes-to-cubes, Borsuk-Ulam/isoperimetry material, and
related probability/topology notes.

## Transcript Status

No official transcript files were found on IHES, Carmin, FGSI/EPFL, CIMS, or
CNRS/CIRM during this search. The official text layer currently found is PDFs,
lecture notes, slides, and event synopses.

The FGSI/EPFL event advertises the "What is Probability?" video at:

https://bernoulli.epfl.ch/images/website/What_is_Probability_v2%282%29.mp4

That endpoint returned HTTP 404 on 2026-05-31, so the video was not downloaded
from EPFL. The associated text material is present through the CIMS/FGSI PDFs.

## Verification Files

- `FILELIST.txt` lists downloaded files and byte sizes.
- `CHECKSUMS.sha256` contains SHA-256 hashes for the corpus.

## Content Relevance

The strongest source match for the requested theme is:

- finite-set and large-set symmetry as a root of probability;
- algebra of subsets in Cartesian products;
- spaces of measurements, partitions, and projections;
- cones of measures;
- entropy and large deviations;
- Pascal recursion and probability/topology notes.

The statement that normalization is secondary is consistent with the
cone/counting-first reading, but no official transcript sentence with that exact
claim was located. Treat that point as an interpretation unless a page or
timestamp is later pinned.
